paragraphs: The Cheesecake Factory Incorporated is a leader in experiential dining. We are culinary forward and relentlessly focused on hospitality. As of February 23, 2026, we owned and operated 368 restaurants throughout the United States and Canada under brands including The Cheesecake Factory® (216 locations), North Italia® (48 locations), Flower Child® (43 locations) and additional brands within our Fox Restaurant Concepts ("Other FRC") portfolio (55 locations). Internationally, 35 The Cheesecake Factory® restaurants operate under licensing agreements. Our bakery division operates two facilities that produce quality cheesecakes and other baked products for our restaurants, international licensees and third-party bakery customers.

Our business originated in 1972 when Oscar and Evelyn Overton founded a small bakery in the Los Angeles area. In 1978, their son, David Overton, our Chairman of the Board and Chief Executive Officer, led the creation and opening of the first The Cheesecake Factory restaurant in Beverly Hills, California. In 1992, the Company was incorporated in Delaware as The Cheesecake Factory Incorporated (referred to herein as the "Company" or as "we," "us" and "our"). Our executive offices are located at 26901 Malibu Hills Road, Calabasas Hills, California 91301, and our telephone number is (818) 871-3000.

We maintain a general website at www.thecheesecakefactory.com, as well as websites for our bakery and other brands, including www.northitalia.com, www.iamaflowerchild.com and www.foxrc.com. Our annual reports on Form 10-K, quarterly reports on Form 10-Q, current reports on Form 8-K, all amendments to those reports and our proxy statements are available on our general website at no charge, as soon as reasonably practicable after these materials are filed with or furnished to the SEC. Our filings are also available on the SEC's website at www.sec.gov. The content of our websites is not incorporated by reference into this Form 10-K.

We utilize a 52/53-week fiscal year ending on the Tuesday closest to December 31 for financial reporting purposes. Fiscal years 2025, 2024 and 2023 each consisted of 52 weeks. Fiscal year 2026 will consist of 52 weeks.

In recent years, our operating results were impacted by geopolitical and macroeconomic events, causing supply chain challenges and significantly increased commodity and wage inflation. Our commodity and wage inflationary environment began returning to more historical levels in fiscal 2024.

The impact of ongoing geopolitical and macroeconomic events, including evolving government policies and global trade and tariff dynamics, could lead to further wage inflation, product and services cost inflation, disruptions in the supply chain, staffing challenges, shifts in consumer behavior, and delays in new restaurant openings. Adverse weather conditions and natural disasters may further exacerbate a number of these factors. Any of these factors may have an adverse impact on our business and materially adversely affect our financial performance.

As of February 23, 2026, we operated 216 The Cheesecake Factory restaurants, which strive to provide a distinctive, high-quality dining experience at moderate prices by offering an extensive, innovative and evolving menu in an upscale casual, high-energy setting with attentive, efficient and friendly service. As a result, The Cheesecake Factory restaurants appeal to a diverse customer base across a broad demographic range. Our extensive menu and strategic selection of locations enable us to compete for substantially all dining preferences and occasions, from the key lunch and dinner day parts to the mid-afternoon and late-night day parts, which are traditionally weaker times for most casual dining restaurants, as well as special occasion dining. The Cheesecake Factory restaurants are generally open seven days a week for lunch and dinner, and we offer additional menu items for weekend brunch.

All of our restaurants offer a full-service bar where our entire menu is served. During fiscal 2025, alcoholic beverage sales represented 11% of The Cheesecake Factory restaurant sales. We offer all items on our menu, except alcoholic beverages where disallowed by regulation, for off-premise consumption, sales of which comprised approximately 21% of The Cheesecake Factory restaurant sales during fiscal 2025. We work with a third party to provide delivery service from all of our locations and offer online ordering for to-go sales at all of our domestic locations.

The Cheesecake Factory menu features approximately 225 items, exclusive of beverage and dessert items and including items presented on supplemental menus, such as our SkinnyLicious® menu that offers innovative items at 590 calories or less. Our menu offerings include appetizers, pizza, seafood, steaks, chicken, burgers, bowls, bites, small plates, pastas, salads, sandwiches and omelettes, including a selection of vegan and gluten-free items.

Our ability to create, promote and attractively display our unique line of desserts is also important to the competitive positioning and financial success of our restaurants. We offer approximately 45 varieties of proprietary cheesecake and other desserts in our restaurants. Our brand identity and reputation for offering premium desserts results in a significant level of dessert sales, representing approximately 17% of The Cheesecake Factory sales during fiscal 2025.

The restaurant industry is comprised of multiple segments, including fine dining, casual dining, fast casual and quick-service. The Cheesecake Factory restaurants operate in the upscale casual dining segment, which is positioned above core casual dining, with standards that are closer to fine dining. Upscale casual dining is differentiated by freshly prepared and innovative food, flavorful recipes with creative presentations, unique restaurant layouts, eye-catching design elements and more personalized service. We believe that we are a leader in upscale casual dining given the historically high average sales per square foot of our restaurants as compared to others in this segment.

The restaurant industry is highly competitive with respect to menu and food quality, service, personnel, location, décor and value. We compete directly and indirectly with national and regional casual dining restaurant chains, as well as independently-owned restaurants. In addition, we face competition from fast casual and quick-service restaurants, grocery stores and meal kits that have increased the quality and variety of their food products in response to consumer demand. We also compete with other restaurants and retail establishments for quality sites and staff and managers to operate our restaurants.
The key elements that drive our total customer experience and help position us from a competitive standpoint include the following:

Extensive and Innovative Menu, Made Fresh from Scratch. Our restaurants offer one of the broadest menus in upscale casual dining and feature a wide array of flavors with portions designed for sharing. In contrast to many restaurant chains, substantially all of our menu items, except those desserts produced at our bakery facilities, are prepared from scratch daily at our restaurants with high-quality, fresh ingredients using innovative and proprietary recipes. We believe one of our competitive strengths is our ability to anticipate customer preferences and adapt our expansive menu to the latest trends. We regularly update our ingredients and cooking techniques, as well as create new menu items and new categories of food offerings at our restaurants, further enhancing the variety, quality and price points offered and keeping our menu relevant to our customers. All new menu items are selected based on anticipated sales popularity and profitability. We also regularly introduce new and innovative cheesecakes and other baked desserts. In 2025, we launched the Peach Perfect with Raspberry Drizzle Cheesecake in conjunction with National Cheesecake Day.

headings: Risks Related to the Restaurant Industry
The impact global and domestic economic conditions have on consumer discretionary spending and our costs of operations could materially adversely affect our financial performance.
Our inability to grow comparable restaurant sales could materially adversely affect our financial performance.
If we are unable to protect our reputation, the value of our brands and sales at our restaurants may be negatively impacted, which could materially adversely affect our financial performance.
In past years we have experienced and may again experience significant labor cost inflation, which has and may in the future significantly increase our cost of doing business.
Labor organizing could harm our operations and competitive position in the restaurant industry, which could materially adversely affect our financial performance.
Our failure to effectively develop, grow and operate North Italia, Flower Child and our other branded concepts could materially adversely affect our financial performance.
Adverse weather conditions, natural disasters and public health emergencies could unfavorably impact our restaurant sales, which could materially adversely affect our financial performance.

Our inability to anticipate and react effectively to changes in the costs of key operating resources may increase our cost of doing business, which could materially adversely affect our financial performance.
Our financial performance could be materially adversely affected if we fail to retain, or effectively respond to a loss of, key executives.
Any inability to effectively use and manage social media could harm our marketing efforts as well as our reputation, which could materially adversely affect our financial performance.
Our failure to adequately protect our intellectual property could materially adversely affect our financial performance.
We face a variety of risks and challenges related to our international operations and global brand development efforts, any of which could materially adversely affect our financial performance.
Our inability to secure an adequate number of high-quality sites for future restaurant openings could adversely affect our ability to grow our business.
We may engage in expansion opportunities or other initiatives which may create risks to our business that could materially adversely affect our financial performance.
If we are unable to manage risks related to our business, costs associated with litigation and insurance could increase, which could materially adversely affect our financial performance.
paragraphs: An investment in our common stock involves risks and uncertainties. In addition to the information contained elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K and other filings that we make with the SEC, you should carefully read and consider the risks described below before making an investment decision. The occurrence of any of the following risks could materially harm our business, operating results, earnings per share, financial position, cash flows and/or the trading price of our common stock (individually and collectively referred to as our "financial performance"). In addition, our actual financial performance could vary materially from any results expressed or implied by forward-looking statements contained in this report, in any of our other filings with the SEC and other communications by us, both written and oral, depending on a variety of factors, including the risks and uncertainties described below. It is not possible for us to predict all possible risk factors or the impact these factors could have on us or the extent to which any one factor, or combination of factors, may materially adversely affect our financial performance. The risk factors set forth below are not guarantees that no such conditions exist as of the date of this report and should not be interpreted as an affirmative statement that such risks or conditions have not materialized, in whole or in part.

Dining out is a discretionary expenditure that is influenced by domestic and global economic conditions, including, but not limited to: geopolitical instability, including armed conflicts, supply shortages, interest rates, changes to the terms of international trade agreements, unemployment, significant cost inflation, public health emergencies, consumer confidence, consumer purchasing and saving habits, credit conditions, stock market performance, home values, population growth, household incomes and tax policy.

Material changes to governmental policy related to domestic and international fiscal concerns, and/or changes in central bank policies with respect to monetary policy, also could affect consumer discretionary spending. Any factor affecting consumer discretionary spending may influence customer traffic in our restaurants and average check amount, thus potentially having a material impact on our financial performance.

In recent years, our operating results were impacted by geopolitical and macroeconomic events, causing supply chain challenges and significantly increased commodity and wage inflation. Our commodity and wage inflationary environment began returning to more historical levels in fiscal 2024. The impact of ongoing geopolitical and macroeconomic events, including evolving government policies, and global trade and tariff dynamics, could lead to further wage inflation, product and services cost inflation, disruptions in the supply chain, staffing challenges, shifts in consumer behavior, and delays in new restaurant openings. Any of these factors may have an adverse impact on our business and materially adversely affect our financial performance.

We strive to increase comparable restaurant sales by improving customer traffic trends and growing average check. Changes in customer traffic and average check amount may be impacted by a variety of factors, including, without limitation: macroeconomic conditions that impact consumer discretionary spending; perception of our concepts' offerings in terms of quality, price, value and service; the competitive environment; changes in consumer eating or drinking habits; the evolving retail landscape, which is becoming increasingly influenced by technology and a growing consumer preference for convenience, value and experience; weather conditions; natural disasters; and demographic, economic and other changes in the trade areas in which our restaurants are located and changes in the regulatory environment. (See the risk factor titled "The impact global and domestic economic conditions have on consumer discretionary spending and our costs of operations could materially adversely affect our financial performance.")

We compete directly and indirectly for customer traffic with national and regional full-service dining restaurant chains as well as independently owned restaurants. In addition, we face competition from fast casual and quick service restaurants, grocery stores and meal kits that have increased the quality and variety of their food products in response to consumer demand. We believe that many consumers remain focused on value and if our competitors promote and deliver a higher degree of perceived value, our customer traffic could suffer.

paragraphs: This Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations ("MD&A"), which contains forward-looking statements, should be read in conjunction with our audited consolidated financial statements and related notes in Part IV, Item 15 of this report, the "Risk Factors" included in Part I, Item 1A of this report and the cautionary statements included throughout this report. The inclusion of supplementary analytical and related information herein may require us to make estimates and assumptions to enable us to fairly present, in all material respects, our analysis of trends and expectations with respect to our results of operations and financial position.

We utilize a 52/53-week fiscal year ending on the Tuesday closest to December 31 for financial reporting purposes. Fiscal years 2025, 2024 and 2023 each consisted of 52 weeks. Fiscal year 2026 will consist of 52 weeks. The following MD&A includes a discussion comparing our results in fiscal 2025 to fiscal 2024. For a discussion comparing our results from fiscal 2024 to fiscal 2023, refer to "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" in Part II, Item 7 of our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024, filed with the SEC on February 24, 2025.

In recent years, our operating results were impacted by geopolitical and macroeconomic events, causing supply chain challenges and significantly increased commodity and wage inflation. Our commodity and wage inflationary environment began returning to more historical levels in fiscal 2024.

The impact of ongoing geopolitical and macroeconomic events, including evolving government policies and global trade and tariff dynamics, could lead to further wage inflation, product and services cost inflation, disruptions in the supply chain, staffing challenges, shifts in consumer behavior, and delays in new restaurant openings. Adverse weather conditions and natural disasters may further exacerbate a number of these factors. Any of these factors may have an adverse impact on our business and materially adversely affect our financial performance.

The Cheesecake Factory Incorporated is a leader in experiential dining. We are culinary forward and relentlessly focused on hospitality. As of February 23, 2026, we owned and operated 368 restaurants throughout the United States and Canada under brands including The Cheesecake Factory® (216 locations), North Italia® (48 locations), Flower Child® (43 locations) and additional brands within our FRC portfolio (55 locations). Internationally, 35 The Cheesecake Factory® restaurants operate under licensing agreements. Our bakery division operates two facilities that produce quality cheesecakes and other baked products for our restaurants, international licensees and third-party bakery customers.

Our strategy is driven by our commitment to deliver exceptional food and hospitality, and is centered primarily on menu innovation, service and operational execution to differentiate our concepts and drive competitively strong performance that is sustainable over the long-term. Financially, we are focused on prudently managing expenses at our restaurants, bakery facilities and corporate support center, while leveraging our scale, purchasing power and operational discipline to support financial performance.

Investing in new Company-owned restaurant development is our top long-term capital allocation priority, with a focus on opening our concepts in premier locations within both new and existing markets. We plan to continue expanding The Cheesecake Factory, North Italia and Flower Child concepts. In addition, our FRC subsidiary serves as an incubator, innovating new food, dining and hospitality experiences to create differentiated, high-quality concepts.
Our revenue growth is primarily driven by new restaurant openings and increases in comparable restaurant sales.

For The Cheesecake Factory concept, our strategy is to increase comparable restaurant sales by growing average check while maintaining customer traffic through (1) continuing to offer innovative, high quality menu items that offer customers a wide range of options in terms of flavor, price and value, (2) focusing on service and hospitality with the goal of delivering an exceptional dining experience and (3) continuing to provide our customers with convenient options for off-premise dining. We are continuing our efforts on a number of initiatives, including menu innovation, increasing customer throughput in our restaurants, leveraging our gift card program, partnering with a third party to provide delivery services for our restaurants, increasing customer awareness of our online ordering capabilities and improving the pick-up experience, augmenting our marketing programs, including our Cheesecake Rewards® program, enhancing our training programs and leveraging insights from our customer satisfaction measurement platform.

Average check variations are driven by menu price increases and/or changes in menu mix. We generally update The Cheesecake Factory menus twice a year, and our philosophy is to use price increases to help offset key operating cost increases in a manner that supports both our margin and customer traffic objectives. Prior to fiscal 2022, we targeted menu price increases of approximately 2% to 3% annually, utilizing a market-based strategy to help mitigate cost pressure in higher-wage geographies. In the last three fiscal years, we implemented price increases above our historical levels, to help offset significant inflationary cost pressures. We will continue to take the cost and inflationary environment into consideration when implementing future pricing decisions. In addition, on a regular basis, we carefully consider opportunities to adjust our menu offerings or ingredients to help manage product availability and cost.

Margins are subject to fluctuations in commodity costs, labor, restaurant-level occupancy expenses, general and administrative ("G&A") expenses and preopening expenses. Our objective is to drive margin expansion over time by leveraging incremental sales to increase restaurant-level margins at The Cheesecake Factory concept, leveraging our bakery operations, international and consumer packaged goods royalty revenue streams and G&A expense, and optimizing our restaurant portfolio.

We plan to employ a balanced capital allocation strategy, comprised of investing in new restaurants that are expected to meet our targeted returns, managing our aggregate debt levels and returning capital to shareholders through our dividend and share repurchase programs, the latter of which offsets dilution from our equity compensation program and supports our earnings per share growth. Future decisions to pay, increase or decrease dividends or to repurchase shares are at the discretion of the Board and will be dependent on a number of factors, including limitations pursuant to the terms and conditions of our Loan Agreement and applicable law.

Longer-term, we believe our domestic revenue growth (comprised of our targeted annual unit growth of 7% in aggregate across concepts and comparable sales growth) combined with margin expansion, planned debt repayments and an anticipated capital return program will support our long-term financial objective of 10% to 15% total return to shareholders, on average. We define our total return as earnings per share growth plus our dividend yield. (See Item 1A — Risk Factors — "Our stock price could be adversely affected if our performance falls short of our financial guidance and/or market expectations.")

paragraphs: The Cheesecake Factory Incorporated 是體驗式用餐的領導者。我們在美食創新方面持續前進，並致力於餐飲服務。截至 2026 年 2 月 23 日，我們在美國與加拿大經營 368 家餐廳，品牌包括 The Cheesecake Factory®（216 家）、North Italia®（48 家）、Flower Child®（43 家）以及 Fox Restaurant Concepts（"Other FRC"）品牌組閤中的其他品牌（55 家）。國際上，35 家 The Cheesecake Factory® 餐廳透過授權協議運作。我們的烘焙部門運作兩處設施，製造高品質的芝士蛋糕及其他烘焙產品，供我們的餐廳、國際授權者及第三方烘焙客戶使用。

本公司業務起源於1972年，當時Oscar與Evelyn Overton在洛杉磯地區創辦了一家小型麵包店。1978年，他們的兒子David Overton，本公司董事長兼首席執行長，領導創辦並開幕了第一家The Cheesecake Factory餐廳，位於加州比佛利山。1992年，本公司在特拉華州註冊為The Cheesecake Factory Incorporated（ herein 簡稱為"本公司"或"我們"、"我們"及"我們"）。本公司總部位於加州卡拉巴薩斯希爾斯的26901 Malibu Hills Road，郵遞區號為91301，電話號碼為(818) 871-3000。

我們維護一個一般網站 www.thecheesecakefactory.com，以及我們烘焙部門及其他品牌的網站，包括 www.northitalia.com、www.iamaflowerchild.com 和 www.foxrc.com。我們的年度報告（Form 10-K）、季報（Form 10-Q）、現況報告（Form 8-K）、所有這些報告的修正案以及我們的代理聲明，可在我們一般網站上免費取得，自這些資料提交或提供給 SEC 後盡速提供。我們的資料也可在 SEC 網站 www.sec.gov 上取得。我們網站的內容未經引用納入本 Form 10-K。
我們採用 52/53 週財務年度，以接近 12 月 31 日的星期二為結算日，用於財務報告。財務年度 2025、2024 和 2023 各為 52 週。財務年度 2026 將為 52 週。
近年來，我們的營運結果受到地緣政治與總體經濟事件的影響，導致供應鏈挑戰及商品與工資通貨膨脹顯著增加。我們的商品與工資通貨膨脹環境在財務年度 2024 開始回復至較歷史水平。
持續的地緣政治與總體經濟事件的影響，包括政府政策的變化及全球貿易與關稅動態，可能導致進一步的工資通貨膨脹、產品與服務成本通貨膨脹、供應鏈中斷、人力配置困難、消費者行為的變化，以及新餐廳開幕的延遲。惡劣天氣與自然災害可能進一步加劇這些因素中的若干項。任何這些因素都可能對我們的業務產生不利影響，並嚴重影響我們的財務表現。

截至 2026 年 2 月 23 日，我們運作 216 家 The Cheesecake Factory 餐廳，致力於提供獨特、高品質的用餐體驗，價格適中，透過提供廣泛、創新且不斷進化的菜單，在高能量的高檔休閒環境中，搭配專注、高效且友善的服務。因此，The Cheesecake Factory 餐廳吸引來自廣泛人口層次的多樣化顧客羣。我們廣泛的菜單與戰略性的門店選擇，使我們能競爭幾乎所有用餐偏好與場合，從關鍵的午餐與晚餐時段，到傳統上較弱的午後與深夜時段，以及特殊場合用餐。The Cheesecake Factory 餐廳通常週一至週日都營業午餐與晚餐，我們在週末提供早餐選項。

我們所有餐廳均設有全服務酒吧，供應我們全部的菜單。在財務年度 2025，酒精飲料銷售佔 The Cheesecake Factory 餐廳銷售的 11%。我們提供所有菜單項目，除了因規範限制而不得供應酒精飲料的項目，供應外場消費，外場銷售佔 The Cheesecake Factory 餐廳銷售的約 21%。我們與第三方合作，提供所有門店的外送服務，並在所有國內門店提供線上訂購服務，以促進外場銷售。
The Cheesecake Factory 餐點選項包含約 225 項商品，不計飲料與甜點項目，並包含補充菜單上的項目，例如我們的 SkinnyLicious® 菜單，提供創新商品，熱量為 590 大卡或以下。我們的餐點選項包括前菜、披薩、海鮮、牛排、雞肉、漢堡、碗裝餐點、小食、小盤餐點、義麵、沙拉、三明治與蛋餅，包含部分素食與無麩質選項。
我們能創造、推廣並吸引人展示我們獨特的甜點系列，對我們餐廳的競爭地位與財務成功至關重要。我們在餐廳內提供約 45 種專利的芝士蛋糕及其他甜點。我們的品牌形象與提供高級甜點的聲譽，導致甜點銷售佔有相當高的比例，約佔 The Cheesecake Factory 營業收入的 17% ，於財務年度 2025 年。

餐飲業包含多個部門，包括高檔餐廳、休閒餐廳、快速休閒餐廳與速食餐廳。The Cheesecake Factory 餐廳運作於高檔休閒餐廳部門，此部門定位在核心休閒餐廳之上，標準更接近高檔餐廳。高檔休閒餐廳的特色為新鮮製作與創新食物、風味濃鬱且有創意的菜單呈現、獨特的餐廳空間設計、吸引目光的設計元素與更個人化的服務。我們相信我們在高檔休閒餐廳部門中為領導者，因為我們餐廳的平均每平方英尺銷售額歷來高於此部門的其他競爭對手。
餐飲業在餐點與食物品質、服務、人力、位置、裝潢與價值方面競爭激烈。我們與全國性與區域性休閒餐廳連鎖品牌，以及獨立經營的餐廳直接與間接競爭。此外，我們也面臨快速休閒與速食餐廳、超市與餐點組合服務的競爭，這些競爭對手因應消費者需求，已提升其食品品質與種類。我們也與其他餐廳與零售場所競爭優質的場地與員工與經理人來經營我們的餐廳。
驅動我們總體顧客體驗並幫助我們在競爭中建立優勢的關鍵要素如下：

廣泛且創新餐點，從頭製作。我們的餐廳提供高檔休閒餐廳中最廣的餐點選項，並具備多樣化的風味與份量設計，適合分享。與許多餐廳連鎖品牌不同，我們幾乎所有餐點（除在烘焙廠製造的甜點外），皆於每日於餐廳內從頭製作，使用高品質的新鮮原料與創新且專利的食譜。我們相信我們的競爭優勢之一，是我們預測顧客偏好並調整我們廣泛的餐點選項以符合最新趨勢的能力。我們定期更新我們的原料與烹飪技術，並在餐廳內創造新的餐點與新的食品類別，進一步提升種類、品質與價格點，並保持我們的餐點選項符合顧客需求。所有新餐點皆根據預期的銷售人氣與獲利潛力進行選擇。我們也定期推出新的創新芝士蛋糕及其他烘焙甜點。於 2025 年，我們配合國家芝士蛋糕日推出了 Peach Perfect with Raspberry Drizzle 芝士蛋糕。

headings: 地緣政治及其他總體經濟影響至我公司營運環境
財務年度 2025 相較於財務年度 2024

paragraphs: 本項「管理層討論與分析」（"MD&A"）包含前瞻性陳述，應與本報告第四部分第十五項所載經審計之合併財務報表及相關附註、本報告第一部分第1A項所載「風險因素」以及本報告中所載警示性陳述一併閱讀。本報告中包含補充性分析及相關資訊，可能需要我們做出估計與假設，以確保我們能就營運結果與財務狀況的趨勢與預期，於所有重大方面做出公平呈現。

我們採用52/53週財務年度，以接近12月31日的星期二為財務報導結算日。財務年度2025、2024及2023各為52週。財務年度2026將為52週。以下MD&A包含比較財務年度2025與財務年度2024的結果討論。如需比較財務年度2024與財務年度2023的結果討論，請參閱我們於2025年2月24日提交至SEC的財務年度終結於2024年12月31日之10-K年度報告，第二部分第7項所載「管理層討論與分析」。
近年來，我們的營運結果受到地緣政治與總體經濟事件的影響，造成供應鏈挑戰與顯著的原材料與工資通貨膨脹。我們的原材料與工資通貨膨脹環境在財務年度2024開始回復至較歷史水平。
持續進行的地緣政治與總體經濟事件的影響，包括政府政策的演變與全球貿易與關稅動態，可能導致進一步的工資通貨膨脹、產品與服務成本通貨膨脹、供應鏈中斷、人力配置困難、消費者行為的變化，以及新餐廳開幕的延遲。惡劣天氣與天然災害可能進一步加劇這些因素中的若干項。任何這些因素都可能對我們的業務產生不利影響，並對我們的財務表現造成重大不利影響。

The Cheesecake Factory Incorporated 是體驗式用餐的領導者。我們以創新料理為核心，並致力於提供卓越的服務與 hospitality。截至2026年2月23日，我們在美國與加拿大擁有並營運368間餐廳，品牌包括 The Cheesecake Factory®（216間）、North Italia®（48間）、Flower Child®（43間）以及我們FRC資產組閤中的其他品牌（55間）。國際上，35間 The Cheesecake Factory® 餐廳透過授權協議運作。我們的烘焙部門運作兩間工廠，生產高品質的芝士蛋糕及其他烘焙產品，供應我們的餐廳、國際授權經銷商與第三方烘焙客戶。
我們的策略由我們致力於提供卓越的餐點與 hospitality 的承諾所驅動，主要聚焦於菜單創新、服務與營運執行，以區隔我們的概念並推動具競爭力且可長久維持的表現。財務方面，我們專注於在餐廳、烘焙工廠與企業支援中心審慎管理費用，同時利用我們的規模、採購力與營運紀律來支撐財務表現。
投資於新 Company-owned 餐廳開發是我們長期資本配置的首要優先事項，重點在於在新舊市場中優質地點開設我們的概念。我們計畫持續擴張 The Cheesecake Factory、North Italia 與 Flower Child 的概念。此外，我們的 FRC 子公司擔任育成中心，創新新穎的餐點、用餐與 hospitality 經驗，以創造區隔且高品質的概念。
我們的營收成長主要由新餐廳開幕與可比餐廳銷售額增加所驅動。

對於 The Cheesecake Factory 概念，我們的策略是透過 (1) 維持顧客人數，同時提高平均消費金額，來增加可比餐廳銷售額，具體做法包括持續提供創新且高品質的餐點選項，讓顧客在風味、價格與價值方面有廣泛選擇、(2) 聚焦服務與待客品質，目標是提供卓越的用餐體驗，以及 (3) 繼續為顧客提供便利的外帶用餐選項。我們正在進行多項計畫，包括餐點創新、提高餐廳內顧客流量、運用我們的禮券計畫、與第三方合作提供餐廳的外送服務、提高顧客對我們線上訂購功能的認知、改善外帶體驗、強化我們的行銷計畫，包括 Cheesecake Rewards® 計畫、提升我們的培訓計畫，並運用來自顧客滿意度測量平台的洞察力。

平均消費金額的變動是由餐點價格上漲及/或餐點組合的變化所驅動。我們通常每年更新 The Cheesecake Factory 的餐點選項兩次，我們的哲學是透過價格上漲來抵消關鍵營運成本的增加，同時支持我們的毛利率與顧客人數目標。在財務年度 2022 年之前，我們目標每年將餐點價格提高約 2% 到 3%，透過市場導向的策略來幫助緩解高工資地區的成本壓力。在最近三個財務年度，我們實施了高於歷史水平的價格上漲，以幫助抵消顯著的通貨膨脹成本壓力。我們將持續考量成本與通貨膨脹環境，以制定未來的定價決策。此外，我們會定期考慮調整餐點選項或食材的機會，以幫助管理產品供應與成本。
毛利率會受到原物料成本、人力、餐廳層面的佔用費用、一般及行政（"G&A"）費用及預開支的波動影響。我們的目標是透過增加餐廳層面的銷售額來提高 The Cheesecake Factory 概念的毛利率，運用我們的烘焙部門、國際及消費者包裝商品 royalty 收入流，以及 G&A 費用，並優化我們的餐廳組合，以實現長期的毛利率擴張。
我們計畫採用平衡的資本配置策略，包括投資預期可達成我們目標回報的新餐廳、管理我們的總債務水準，以及透過股息與股票回購計畫將資本回饋給股東，後者可抵消我們員工持股計畫所造成的稀釋，並支持我們每股盈餘的成長。未來是否發放、提高或降低股息，或是否回購股票的決定，皆由董事會酌情決定，並會根據多種因素，包括根據我們貸款協議的條款與條件及適用法律的限制。

從長遠來看，我們相信我們的國內營收成長（包含我們目標每年在各概念中總體單位成長 7% 以及可比銷售額成長）與毛利率擴張、預計的債務償還計畫以及預期的資本回饋計畫，將支持我們長期的財務目標，即平均達成 10% 到 15% 的總股東回報率。我們將總回報定義為每股盈餘成長加上我們的股息收益率。（請參閱項目 1A — 風險因素 — "若我們的表現未達我們的財務指引及/或市場預期，我們的股票價格可能會受到不利影響。")

headings: 全球及國內經濟條件對消費者可支配所得及我們營運成本的影響，可能對我們的財務表現造成重大不利影響。
我們若無法成長同店銷售額，可能對我們的財務表現造成重大不利影響。
若我們無法保護我們的聲譽，將可能影響我們品牌價值及餐廳銷售額，這可能對我們的財務表現造成重大不利影響。
過去幾年我們曾經歷並可能再次經歷顯著的勞動成本上漲，這已並可能未來顯著提高我們的營運成本。
勞動組織化可能損害我們在餐飲業的營運及競爭地位，這可能對我們的財務表現造成重大不利影響。
我們若無法有效開發、成長及營運 North Italia、Flower Child 及我們其他品牌概念，可能對我們的財務表現造成重大不利影響。
不利天氣條件、自然災害及公共衛生緊急事件可能不利影響我們的餐廳銷售額，這可能對我們的財務表現造成重大不利影響。
與我們業務相關的風險
我們若無法有效預測並應對關鍵營運資源成本的變動，可能會提高我們的營運成本，這可能會對我們的財務表現造成重大不利影響。
若我們無法留住關鍵高階主管，或對其離職無法有效應對，可能會對我們的財務表現造成重大不利影響。
若無法有效運用及管理社交媒體，可能會影響我們的行銷成效及聲譽，這可能會對我們的財務表現造成重大不利影響。
我們若無法充分保護智慧財產權，可能會對我們的財務表現造成重大不利影響。
我們在國際營運及全球品牌發展方面面臨多種風險與挑戰，任何一種都可能對我們的財務表現造成重大不利影響。
我們若無法取得足夠數量的高品質場地用以未來餐廳開店，可能會影響我們擴張業務的能力。
我們可能參與擴張機會或其他計畫，這些計畫可能對我們的業務造成風險，這可能會對我們的財務表現造成重大不利影響。

paragraphs: 投資本公司普通股涉及風險與不確定性。除本年度10-K表報表及其他向美國證券交易委員會（SEC）提交之文件所載資訊外，您應仔細閱讀並考量下列所列風險，以作為投資決策之參考。上述任何風險之發生，可能會對本公司之業務、營運成果、每股盈餘、財務狀況、現金流及/或普通股之交易價格（單獨或合併稱為「財務表現」）造成重大影響。此外，本公司實際財務表現可能與本報告或其他向SEC提交之文件及其它通訊中所表達或暗示之預測結果有重大差異，此乃因多種因素影響，包括下列所列風險與不確定性。本公司無法預測所有可能之風險因素，或這些因素對本公司之影響，亦無法預測任何單一因素或因素組合對本公司財務表現造成重大不利影響之程度。下列所列風險因素並非保證截至本報告日不存在任何此類情況，亦不應被解釋為明確表示此類風險或情況未完全或部分實現。
外出用餐為一種選擇性支出，受國內與國際總體經濟條件影響，包括但不限於：地緣政治不穩定，包括軍事衝突、供應短缺、利率、國際貿易協議條款之變更、失業率、重大成本通貨膨脹、公共衛生危機、消費者信心、消費者購買新趨勢與儲蓄習慣、信貸條件、股市表現、房價、人口成長、家庭收入與稅收政策。
與國內外財政議題相關之政府政策變更，以及央行針對貨幣政策之政策變動，也可能影響消費者選擇性支出。任何影響消費者選擇性支出的因素，可能會影響本公司餐廳之顧客人數與平均消費金額，進而對本公司財務表現造成重大影響。

近年來，本公司營運成果受到地緣政治與總體經濟事件之影響，導致供應鏈挑戰與顯著增加之原材料與工資通貨膨脹。本公司之原材料與工資通貨膨脹環境，自財務年度2024年起開始回歸至較歷史水平。持續進行之地緣政治與總體經濟事件，包括政府政策之演變，以及全球貿易與關稅動態，可能導致進一步之工資通貨膨脹、產品與服務成本通貨膨脹、供應鏈中斷、人力配置困難、消費者行為轉變，以及新餐廳開幕之延遲。上述任何因素都可能對本公司業務造成不利影響，並對本公司財務表現造成重大不利影響。

本公司致力於透過改善顧客人數趨勢與提高平均消費金額，來提升同店銷售額。顧客人數與平均消費金額之變動，可能受到多種因素影響，包括但不限於：影響消費者選擇性支出之總體經濟條件；消費者對本公司概念之產品在品質、價格、價值與服務之看法；競爭環境；消費者飲食或飲料習慣之變動；零售業態之演變，該業態正逐漸受到科技與消費者對便利性、價值與體驗之偏好所影響；天氣條件；自然災害；以及本公司餐廳所在商圈之人口、經濟及其他變動，以及監管環境之變動。（請參閱標題為「全球與國內總體經濟條件對消費者選擇性支出與本公司營運成本之影響，可能對本公司財務表現造成重大不利影響」之風險因素。）
本公司與全國性與區域性全服務餐飲連鎖餐廳，以及獨立經營之餐廳，直接與間接競爭顧客人數。此外，本公司亦面臨快速餐飲與速食餐廳、超市與餐點組合服務之競爭，這些競爭對手已因應消費者需求，提高其食品產品之品質與種類。本公司認為許多消費者仍重視價值，若競爭對手能提供更高程度之感知價值，本公司之顧客人數可能受到影響。
